title: staggered-kv-warmup-and-decode-handshake-to-reduce-prefill-burst-jitter
author: Lena Zhou
description:
Motivation: production workloads show intermittent token-level tail spikes when many concurrent prefill requests attempt to hot-prime the KV cache at the same time. Spiky KV priming increases decode jitter and occasionally pushes requests over latency SLOs. Goal: reduce prefill burst jitter without increasing mean latency or adding heavy serialization.

What this PR does (single-string summary): introduce a staggered per-microbatch KV warmup offset, add a lightweight decode-handshake (2-token soft barrier) that enables safe interleaving of prefill and decode stages, and extend the scheduler with a small credit-based backpressure knob that prefers staggered prefill windows for latency-sensitive routes.

Design notes and rationale: the approach intentionally avoids strict serialization between prefill and decode; instead we: 1) compute a deterministic offset for each microbatch using request hash + configurable stride to scatter KV priming across a small time window (default 6-12ms) so that multiple prefill-heavy arrivals aren’t synchronized; 2) add a non-blocking handshake where the prefill stage returns an early 'ready-for-decode' token after priming critical prefixes (first 2 tokens), allowing the decode stage to start generating while the KV warmup continues in the background for long contexts; 3) expose a scheduler hint (prefill_stagger_ratio) and a credit token mechanism per route so critical low-p99 routes get preferentially staggered windows and credits avoid accidental reentrancy bursts.

Implementation highlights: changes touch the serving scheduler, runtime prefill pipeline, kernel priming logic, and observability hooks. Key new modules: scheduler/prefill_staggerer (algorithm + config), runtime/kv_warmup/offset_priming (deterministic offset generator + randomized jitter fallback), runtime/decode/handshake (soft barrier and token exchange), and metrics/runtime_prefill_jitter and metrics/scheduler_prefill_stagger_ratio.

Compatibility and safety: default behavior is conservative (staggering disabled for routes with very short sequence lengths). All knobs are runtime-configurable via the existing route config proto; safe defaults chosen after internal perf runs. Added unit and integration tests cover deterministic offset behavior and handshake timeout/fast-paths.

Benchmark summary: microbenchmarks on p4d (internal harness) show 8-18% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads at 75% load with no regression in median latency or throughput. KV priming CPU overhead is +1.9% on average due to offset accounting; scheduler overhead is negligible (microsecond-scale).

Operational notes: added two new metrics and one debug flag (enable_prefill_staggering) available via runtime flags. Recommended rollout: enable staging with enable_prefill_staggering=false for canary, then flip on for specific low-p99 routes and monitor metrics/runtime_prefill_jitter and per-route cost.

Related: this complements earlier work on kv-prefetch strategies and prefill windowing; see ENG-3149 for rollout plan and ENG-3161 for dashboarding.

- [x] integration tests for mixed prefill/decode flows
- [x] basic perf runs attached to PR
- [x] runtime flag and route config knobs

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can we get a quantified regression budget for median latency? Also please add an opt-out path for the tiny routes we discussed.
Lena Zhou (author): Added median latency check to the CI perf job and route-level opt-out via route_config.proto default false for sequences < 64 tokens.
Ayesha Kapoor: The deterministic offset seems fine but we saw a corner case with identical request hashes from replayed traffic. Can we add fallback randomized jitter?
Lena Zhou (author): Implemented jitter fallback (bounded < 2ms) when offset collisions are detected in a short window; added unit test to simulate collisions.
Samir Patel: Please surface the new metrics in the console dashboards before merge so SRE can monitor. Also confirm there is no unsafe blocking in hot paths.
Lena Zhou (author): Metrics are wired and dashboard PR queued (ENG-3161). Handshake is non-blocking on fast path; added microbench that asserts no syscall in critical loop.
release_notes: Introduce staggered KV warmup and a lightweight decode handshake to reduce prefill burst jitter; exposes runtime flags and metrics. Recommended staged rollout for latency-sensitive routes.
